title: Quantitative Tor bounds under shifts and isomorphisms on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and $A$ an arbitrary commutative ring. Work on the small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with its constant sheaf of rings $A_Y$ and the unbounded derived category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Use the K-flat derived tensor product [def-weil-derived-tensor] and cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, every sheaf $N$ of $A_Y$-modules placed in degree zero, and integers $i,m$, there are isomorphisms, natural in $K$ and $N$,
$$
 (K[m])\otimes_A^L N\cong(K\otimes_A^L N)[m],\qquad
 \mathcal H^i((K[m])\otimes_A^L N)\cong\mathcal H^{i+m}(K\otimes_A^L N).
$$
For any integers $a\leq b$, $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ if and only if $K[m]$ has Tor amplitude in $[a-m,b-m]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. If $K\cong L$, then $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ if and only if $L$ does. Moreover $0\otimes_A^L N\cong0$ for every $N$, and the zero object has Tor amplitude in $[0,0]$. No constructibility or finiteness assumption on $A$ or $K$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated to R=A_Y on the coefficient-sized small model. Its CommShift₂Int structure gives the first-variable shift isomorphisms and naturality in the second variable. Form the natural isomorphism on D(R) × D(R), checking naturality by the fixed-variable shift naturality square and commShift_flip_map. Restrict the second variable along N ↦ Q(N[0]). This gives the tensor shift isomorphism natural in both K and N.

Whisker the tensor shift isomorphism by H^i, reassociate composition, and whisker the natural cohomology shift isomorphism H^i(T[m]) ≅ H^(i+m)(T) of lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift. The indexing identity m+i=i+m follows from commutativity.

Use the proved coefficient-model criterion lem-pe-coefficient-tor-flat-model to represent an object of amplitude [a,b] by a flat complex P zero below a and above b. P[m] has flat terms and is zero below a-m and above b-m. The localization shift isomorphism identifies Q(P[m]) with K[m]. The criterion gives the forward amplitude implication. Apply the same construction with -m and the inverse-shift isomorphism K[m][-m] ≅ K for the converse; both interval endpoints simplify back to a and b.

Unfold HasCoefficientModelTorAmplitude. For an isomorphism e:K≅L, a K-flat representative QP≅L gives QP≅K by composition with e inverse, and a representative of K gives one of L by composition with e. The tensor-test vanishing assertion is identical in each case. Thus the predicates are equivalent.

By the proved flat-K-flat representative existence in lem-pe-coefficient-tor-flat-model, choose a flat-term K-flat representative P of N[0]. Translate its monoidal flatness to the explicit site-flatness via the canonical tensor comparison. The fixed-tensor theorem says that - tensor QP is triangulated and hence preserves zero morphisms and zero objects. Transport that property along the functor isomorphism induced by QP≅N[0]; its value at zero is therefore zero. Separately the zero complex is a flat complex concentrated in [0,0], and Q preserves its zero object. Applying the flat-model criterion proves amplitude [0,0] for zero.
